summary.motive: Use full-field jet sweep action to pull both linebackers and the free safety downhill, then hit a deep post behind the displaced coverage.
summary.whyItWorks: The jet motion commits the RCB and both linebackers before the snap cadence finishes, the mesh-point fake holds the FS downhill through his run fit, and the post breaks over the top precisely when his leverage is worst.
summary.failureMode: A FS who reads mesh-point-to-launch footwork rather than the run fake stays on top and squeezes the post window shut — one disciplined safety erases the entire concept.

beats.title: 1. Jet Sweep Pulls the Trigger Men
beats.text: Z crosses at full speed and every force defender keys him: RCB sprints across the formation, WILL flows hard, and the FS starts creeping downhill. The decoy is doing real work before any fake is even made.

beats.title: 2. Mesh Point Sell
beats.text: The QB opens away and presents a genuine-looking exchange at the mesh point while RB sells the kick-out. At full speed this is indistinguishable from Payton’s actual jet sweep package.

beats.title: 3. Safety Bites, Post Breaks
beats.text: The FS is four yards downhill and gaining — fully committed to sweep fits — exactly when X breaks the post inside off an outside stem. The LCB is still leaning on outside leverage he no longer owns.

beats.title: 4. Launch Over the Top
beats.text: The QB resets his feet and launches with the interior pressure arriving a half-beat late. The throw clears the dragged SS and NICKEL, who spent the play chasing the crossing route.

beats.title: 5. Catch Behind the Recovery
beats.text: X secures the catch at sixteen-plus yards over the recovering FS’s shoulder. The defense traded its two deepest defenders for a fake run to the wrong hash.

relations.tell: Z carries a true full-field sweep path across the formation while X stems outside then stacks a deep post — the only deep route on the call.
